name: Slovenia

train.sum: Ljubljana railway station is the main hub of Slovenske zeleznice (SZ), next to the main bus station. It has fast InterCity and ICS Pendolino trains to Maribor, regional trains across the country and international trains to Croatia, Austria, Italy and Germany. The station area is being rebuilt, so platforms and layout can change.
train.sched: Regional and InterCity trains run from early morning to late evening, usually every 1 to 2 hours on the main lines. A new timetable starts on 13 December 2026. From February to July 2027 the Zurich and Stuttgart night trains are diverted and skip Ljubljana.
tickets: Single fares depend on distance and train type. IC, ICS, EC and EN trains cost extra on top of the ticket
ICS Pendolino to Maribor: seat reservation is compulsory and included in the fare
Slovenia-wide IJPP tickets for trains and buses: day ticket up to 18 EUR, 3-day up to 22 EUR, week up to 36 EUR
Ljubljana to Zagreb: about 9 EUR in 2nd class on regional trains, no seat reservation needed
Austria: ticket to Villach and Graz is cheapest in advance through OBB
train.tip: Buy before you board. If you get on at a station where the ticket office is open and have no ticket, you pay about 12 EUR extra on the train.
buy: Ticket offices at Ljubljana station and other stations
Grem z vlakom app or the SZ website
On the train: possible, but with a surcharge of about 12 EUR if the ticket office at your station was open
International tickets: SZ international ticket offices. Full price tickets only on board and only to the border station
Austria: oebb.at. Hungary: MAV. Germany: Deutsche Bahn

destinations.note: Station for Lake Bled, then about 4 km by bus
Regional trains take about 1 h 15 min
Via Kranj and Jesenice, a train every 2 hours. This station is on the lakeside
Scenic Bohinj line via Radovljica and Bled Jezero
About 4 trains a day on a scenic line to the coast
About 5 trains a day, some run only on Fridays or Sundays
A few trains a day, one continues to Udine
Cross-border train via Maribor, check the timetable for the daily times
Night train, also runs on to Germany and Switzerland
Daytime EuroCity through the Alps, trackwork changes the route from February 2027
One direct train a day via Maribor and Graz
One direct train a day via Celje and Maribor. Track works can replace part of the route with a bus, so check your date
Night train from Zagreb, reservation required

tram.sum: Ljubljana has no trams or metro. The city bus network of LPP is the main public transport and covers all of the city, which is one fare zone. A funicular goes up to Ljubljana Castle.
tram.sched: City buses run from about 03:30 until about midnight. There are no night buses.
tickets: Single ride: 1.50 EUR. With an Urbana card or the Urbana app it is valid for 90 minutes with free transfers
Paying with a Visa or Mastercard bank card is also 1.50 EUR, but it gives no free transfer
Longer rides: 2.50 EUR for two zones and 3.50 EUR for three zones
Urbana card: 2 EUR for the card plus credit up to 50 EUR. You get the 2 EUR back if you return it to a tourist information centre with the receipt
Ljubljana Card: unlimited city bus rides plus sights. 24 hours 41 EUR, 48 hours 49 EUR, 72 hours 54 EUR for adults
Fine without a valid ticket: 100 EUR. A fine of 15 EUR applies to small lapses such as forgetting to validate
tram.tip: Board at the front door and validate your Urbana card, app or bank card at every boarding. If you pay with a bank card, tell the driver when you pay for more than one person.
buy: Tap a Visa or Mastercard bank card, phone or watch on the validator when you board
Urbana card from LPP ticket offices, tourist information centres, newsstands, tobacconists and post offices
Top up the Urbana card with cash or card at the green Urbanomat machines at bus stops
Urbana app (tickets and Ljubljana Card)
Ljubljana Card online, in the Urbana app, or at the tourist information centre and Ljubljana Airport
Not possible to pay by phone call, this service has ended

bus.sum: Ljubljana main bus station is beside the railway station. Nomago, FlixBus and other companies run coaches across Slovenia and to Croatia, Italy and Austria.
bus.sched: Coaches run from early morning to evening, with the most services on weekdays. Check the operator's timetable for the day you travel.
tickets: Slovenia-wide IJPP day ticket for buses and trains: up to 18 EUR
Fares depend on distance and operator, check the operator's site for your trip
City bus fares apply for the nearby towns: 2.50 EUR for two zones and 3.50 EUR for three zones
Pay for city buses with an Urbana card, the app or a bank card
Long distance: book coaches online in advance for the best price
bus.tip: Coaches and trains leave from the same area. The station is being rebuilt, so allow extra time to find your stop.
buy: Ticket counters at the bus station
Online with the coach operator
Some routes sell tickets on board, check the operator
IJPP tickets: non-personal chip card from a station ticket office, then load the ticket online
City buses: Urbana card, app or bank card

airport.sum: Ljubljana Jože Pucnik Airport (LJU) is at Brnik, about 20 km north of the city. There is no train. Buses, shuttles and taxis link it to the centre.
airport.sched: Buses run about every hour from the bus station on weekdays, from about 05:00 to 21:00, and less often at weekends. Buses and shuttles run from early morning to about 21:00.
tickets: Nomago bus from the bus station: about 4 EUR one way, 30 to 60 minutes
Shuttle (GoOpti, Nomago, Markun Shuttle): about 9 to 12 EUR, book in advance
Taxi: about 25 to 35 EUR, about 30 minutes
Ljubljana Card is sold at the airport
airport.tip: Late flights often arrive after the last regular bus, so book a shuttle for evening arrivals.
link: THE Slovenia: How to get to Ljubljana Airport
buy: Bus: online, at the bus station ticket counters, or from the driver
Shuttle: online in advance with GoOpti or the operator's site
Taxi: rank outside the terminal, or book ahead
Bank cards are accepted on public airport buses

metro.note: Ljubljana has no metro and no trams. City buses (LPP) run all routes, and a funicular goes to the castle.
lines: City buses (LPP): the whole City of Ljubljana is fare zone 1
Buses run from about 03:30 to midnight and there are no night buses
Lines 2, 9, 25 and 27 serve the station area, which is being rebuilt
A funicular runs to Ljubljana Castle from the old town

tips: Ljubljana's old town is small and mostly car-free, so many visitors walk or use a bike instead of the bus.
Use an Urbana card or the app for free transfers within 90 minutes. A bank card gives no free transfer.
The fine without a valid bus ticket is 100 EUR since April 2026. Always validate.
The railway and bus station are being rebuilt, so allow extra time to find your platform.
